_comment: Which upstream Astryx components have a hand-written OCaml/Bonsai port, and where it lives. This file is the single human-editable input to tools/gen-port-status.py, which injects the status into docs/components/<Name>.md and writes docs/PORT-STATUS.md. Keep it in sync when a component lands.

infrastructure.name: Common
infrastructure.note: spacing scale, size values, alignment, shared attrs

infrastructure.name: DialogHeader
infrastructure.note: the component that names a dialog: a focusable h2 carrying the id the dialog is told to name itself from, an optional subtitle, start/end slots, an optional divider and a close button rendered only when there is an on_open_change to report to. Not one of registry.json's 103 extracted components, so it does not move the coverage count — it is counted here, with a reason, exactly as registry.json requires.

infrastructure.name: FieldLabel
infrastructure.note: the label and description group, rendered by Field and used on its own by the controls that want the label beside their control rather than above it. It is not one of the extracted 103: upstream's Field/index.ts exports it as part of Field, and the component extraction that gives FieldStatus its own page does not list it (the same extraction merges HStack and VStack into Stack). It is therefore not counted in the coverage numbers, and the coverage generator would flag it as an inconsistency if it were claimed there.

infrastructure.name: InputGroupText
infrastructure.note: Not one of the 103: a text adornment for InputGroup, registered like DialogHeader because it is a rendered component the appearance contract should account for but the coverage denominator should not.

infrastructure.name: Menu_focus
infrastructure.note: the DOM-driven menu navigation ported from upstream's useListFocus/useTypeahead: item selector with boundary scoping, wrap and disabled-skipping, typeahead with a 750 ms reset and same-character cycling, activation carrying the key's modifiers, and the one-frame focus move

infrastructure.name: MetadataListItem
infrastructure.note: one term and its value; renders the pair as a fragment so the list grid decides whether they sit side by side or stacked

infrastructure.name: Tokens
infrastructure.note: generated by tools/gen-ocaml-tokens.py from upstream tokens.stylex.ts

infrastructure.name: Overflow_math
infrastructure.note: the pure fit arithmetic behind an overflowing list: how many items fit, and how many rows they occupy. It is not a component and not one of registry.json's 103, so it moves no coverage number - it is recorded here, with a reason, because the generator would rightly flag a module claimed as ported without being in the registry. Upstream keeps it in a file of its own, with no DOM and no React, so it can be tested in isolation; that is why it was ported before the component and the hook that measure for it. Its cases are driven in the component gate as rows carrying both the expectation and the answer, and they pin the rules rather than the happy path: the floor winning over a lower ceiling, the reserved overflow indicator changing the answer, a ceiling above the item count being a no-op, the multi-row packing, and collapse-from-start keeping the opposite end.

milestones.name: layout + text slice
milestones.note: Compiles, links to js_of_ocaml, and passes the DOM harness (tools/visual/verify-dom.mjs).

milestones.name: layout primitives
milestones.note: Center, Section, Grid and VisuallyHidden — all Class A (no hooks, no measurement).

milestones.name: appearance contract
milestones.note: docs/visual/ — every declaration of every ported component resolved from the stylesheet to a literal, plus the image prompts derived from it (tools/gen-visual-contract.mjs).

milestones.name: showcase site + real-browser gate
milestones.note: site/ renders every ported component; tools/visual/verify-browser.mjs loads it in Chromium over HTTP and clicks a ported Button into Bonsai state. Cross-checked through opencli.

milestones.name: inline + quote content
milestones.note: IconButton (a Button preset, so it keeps Button's marker and its accessible-name contract), Code (a real <code> element) and Blockquote (a bare <cite>, never a <footer>).

milestones.name: component tests in OCaml
milestones.note: test/rt_test.ml builds each component in isolation and dispatches real events via Bonsai_web_test.Handle; test/run.mjs asserts on the DOM. Also the milestone for the HStack/VStack/AspectRatio trio.

milestones.name: wayfinding + empty states
milestones.note:
NavIcon, EmptyState and Citation — all Class A. NavIcon is a single styled span; EmptyState renders role=status with a real heading and a
description (a

cannot hold block children); Citation is the first port that carries a security control, porting upstream's safeUrl check literally (control characters stripped before inspection, javascript:/vbscript:/data:text/html refused) and rendering inert text rather than a link when a URL is refused.

milestones.name: the icon set (generated)
milestones.note: Icon, with its glyph table generated from upstream's defaultIcons.tsx and globalIconRegistry.tsx by tools/extract-icons.mjs. 30 glyphs, 29 of them IconName. The generator refuses to write a partial table and refuses attributes outside an explicit allow-list, because a renamed attribute is silently ignored by the DOM rather than reported.

milestones.name: field status + entry animations
milestones.note: FieldStatus (attached/detached, three types) plus Entry_animation, the port's first time-aware piece: upstream suppresses the entry animation for anything present on the first paint, which is reproduced with a requestAnimationFrame flag read when a view is built. The announcer becomes a role on the container (alert for an error, status otherwise).

milestones.name: the menu-button core (DropdownMenu, phase 1)
milestones.note: DropdownMenu phase 1: the APG menu-button core — trigger ARIA, a surface that is always in the DOM and closed with [hidden] so aria-controls never dangles, rows as menuitems with headings, dividers, groups, a disabled row and an href row that is the anchor itself, Enter/Space activation carrying the key's modifiers, and Menu_focus, the navigation ported from upstream's useListFocus/useTypeahead. Navigation is DOM-driven, as upstream's is: the highlight *is* DOM focus and a disabled row is excluded by the selector, so no index can ever point at an unfocusable row. Every focus move waits a frame, because Bonsai's Effect.Focus.on_activate fires when a computation activates rather than when the rows appear — which is why the keyboard and the focus return are asserted in the browser gate and not in jsdom. Phase 2 (the inline-flyout system, the bottom sheet and the native popover model) is deferred; MoreMenu wraps this.

milestones.name: the form-control core (Field + TextInput, phase 1)
milestones.note: Field is the wrapper every input renders through — label, description and status — and TextInput is the first control that uses it. The wiring is the work: a real <label for>, one name and never two (no aria-labelledby alongside it), aria-describedby listing only the text that is actually rendered, aria-required that agrees with the visible marker, aria-invalid for an error but not a warning, and three placements for a status message (attached behind the control's bottom edge, detached below the field, and tooltip, which renders no message box and announces the message instead). FieldStatus gained the third placement as a type, Icon gained the inherit colour the label icon needs, and every callback is a value in the graph so a state setter can be passed straight in. Deferred with reasons: the loading spinner, the disabled-message tooltip, InputGroup membership and the async changeAction.

milestones.name: the rest of the basic controls (TextArea, phase 1)
milestones.note: The rest of the basic controls, and M13 folded the last two into one milestone: CheckboxInput (a controlled checkbox whose checked and indeterminate states are DOM *properties*, and which cancels a refused click because React restores a controlled input after every event and Vdom does not), Switch (a native checkbox wearing role=switch, with no aria-checked shadowing its own checkedness) and Indicator (one module with three kinds — check, checkbox and radio — the same judgment as HStack/VStack becoming Stack). TextArea opened the milestone by moving the family contract into Input_types; upstream's InputStatus.message being optional was a real gap the move corrected.

milestones.name: the forms layer's edges
milestones.note: RadioList (the first real consumer of the group-label path M12 built, and the milestone where to ask what the platform already does paid off: three radios sharing a name are already one tab stop whose arrows move *and* select, so the port writes no keydown handler at all), FormLayout (upstream's defaultOptionality arrives through React context, which has no analogue here because a child is already built before the container is applied — so it becomes ?optionality per field, and the resolved rule is aria-required = !is_optional && (is_required || default = required), with the layout default moving only aria-required and never the native attribute so it cannot switch on browser validation), and Tooltip — which the plan first put here and which turned out to depend on Layer, so it opened the overlay pillar instead and followed DropdownMenu's convention of a positioned element rather than a top-layer portal. Two divergences are named in tooltip.mli: the message is positioned in place, and the 200 ms hover delay is NOT a divergence — it was recorded as one on the false premise that no timer's callback can write back into the graph, and Gate 23 retired that: Vdom.Attr.create_hook plus a unit Effect.t in a hook's input is exactly that mechanism, and the delay is ported and pressed by the browser gate (it must not open straight away, it must open after the pause, and leaving early must cancel). The milestone also retires the disabledMessage deferral, which turned out not to be a Tooltip at all: the reason must be described for as long as the control is disabled rather than only while hovered, so the controls trade the native disabled attribute for aria-disabled plus form="" and the visual half is one CSS rule — which keeps their stateless signatures.

milestones.name: the overlay pillar opens (Dialog, AlertDialog, DialogHeader)
milestones.note: Dialog is built on the platform's own <dialog>, opened with showModal(), so the top layer, the inert page behind it, the focus trap and the ::backdrop are the browser's rather than the port's — the same judgment as porting a native radio group with no keydown handler. The opening is driven by the hook Gate 23 unlocked: is_open is a value and showModal/close have to follow it, and no event fires when a caller changes their own state, so the DOM side cannot live in a handler. The dismissal matrix is what the port owns and what the browser gate presses: info closes on Escape and on a backdrop click, form closes on Escape but not on a backdrop click, and required refuses both and carries role=alertdialog. Closing from inside closes through <form method="dialog"> — the platform's own mechanism — and the component reports it through on_open_change, which is why the children stay plain nodes. Deferred with reasons: upstream's Layer depth stack, page scroll lock, modal outlet and directional open animation; AlertDialog is ported too, and it is the one that made Dialog's children a tree: it composes Dialog and wires a callback into its own content, which a plain list cannot do. It also overrode the role, which is why Dialog.view takes ~role — the modal form is an alertdialog and the non-modal inline preview says group, because an alertdialog role would promise an interruption and a focus trap the preview does not have. One divergence of mechanism is recorded: upstream reads the viewport in JavaScript (useMediaQuery, 640px) and swaps the two answers, where the port uses one CSS rule (column-reverse) that does the same with no re-render. useImperativeAlertDialog is not ported and the reason is in alert_dialog.mli: it needs a handle concept — code that is not a view asking a mounted component a question — which this port does not have. DialogHeader completes the milestone: the heading carries the id a dialog names itself from (the caller passes the same string to Dialog ~labelled_by, because the caller is the only thing that can see both), and the close button is rendered exactly when there is an ~on_open_change to report to — upstream's rule, since a control that cannot tell anyone it was pressed does nothing. One accessibility behaviour is NOT ported and is named rather than approximated: upstream focuses the title when a modal dialog opens, which matters because the platform's own focus delegate skips a tabindex=-1 element and lands on the close button, so a screen reader would announce Close rather than the dialog's name. The mechanism exists (Menu_focus.focus_on_next_frame, and the hook shape Delay_hook established) but the header does not know the dialog opened — upstream learns it from context — so the fix belongs in Dialog, which does know.

milestones.name: the two halves of a shortcut
milestones.note: Kbd. The interesting part is not the glyphs but the split between them: the wrapper is role=img with an aria-label built from spoken words and every cap inside is aria-hidden, because glyphs are announced meaninglessly and a shortcut can look perfect while being unusable. mod is platform-dependent, which is the one place this port deliberately diverges: upstream defers the answer through useSyncExternalStore to keep a server render and the first client render from disagreeing, and this port has no server render, so it asks directly and records that. The detection rules are upstream's verbatim, including the part that is easy to get wrong: an empty or Unknown client-hints platform is no answer rather than a negative one. The three pure functions are exposed on purpose — the gate runs on Linux, so the Mac branch has to be pressable without a Mac.

milestones.name: buttons joined into one surface
milestones.note: ButtonGroup. Two parts, and only one of them was expected. The connected look is drawn by CSS from the group rather than by a context the children read, because a child in this port is built before its container ever sees it - and the rule has to target the button *inside* each child, since a member that renders its own layer wraps its button, so `> .astryx-button` would miss it and the group would lose its end caps. Upstream hit the same wall and moved those rules out of the group and into Button.tsx; this arrives at the same place from the other side. The part that was not expected: a single tab stop with the arrows moving within it is behaviour, and unlike a radio group the platform does not provide it for buttons, so the group implements the APG roving tabindex itself, and every arrow movement rewrites tabindex on the members - the focused one becomes 0 and the rest -1, which is what makes the next Tab leave the group. Upstream's three useListFocus settings are copied verbatim because all three are load-bearing: the item selector must not key off a tabindex value (the roving stamps one on every item, so `[tabindex="0"]` would drop each member the moment it is stamped -1), the ends wrap, and the nearest boundary above a key event has to be the group's own root, which is what keeps a member's open layer from losing its arrow keys and, in the other direction, keeps a group rendered inside a Popover working. One thing is not ported and is named rather than approximated: size does not propagate from the group to its members, because there is no context to carry it.

milestones.name: a layer anchored to its trigger
milestones.note: Popover. This component is mostly a wrapper around two mechanisms that were ported and proven on their own first (Gates 29 and 30), which was the point of doing them separately: the surface's show/hide with the platform's dismissal reported back to the application, and the trigger's ARIA with its click. What is left in the component is the labelled surface, the generated close control, the focus rule, and the width/padding seam. The focus rule is upstream's exactly: focus enters the first genuine control in the content, falling back to the labelled surface when there is none, and the generated close button is deliberately not a candidate - it sits outside the content wrapper, which is what keeps it out of initial focus while leaving it reachable by keyboard. Closing returns focus to the trigger, but only if focus was inside, so a dismissal the person did not ask for cannot yank focus out of wherever they had moved it. Focus is asked for on the next frame because the surface is display:none until the layer mechanism shows it, and the two hooks run in unspecified order after the same DOM patch - the same ordering trap the dialog hit with showModal. Upstream's light dismiss and Escape are one popover attribute, so asking for one without the other is not expressible here and the port takes the reading that keeps the surface alive until the application closes it, which the mli states. Three things upstream has are named as missing rather than approximated: width is handed to CSS rather than measured and clamped against the viewport (so the surface flips or slides nowhere), there is no modal focus trap (isModal is announced with aria-modal and nothing is trapped), and the render-prop and anchorRef trigger modes have no equivalent in a language without render props - give the trigger a real button and the automatic mode is enough.

milestones.name: a duration that stays readable without re-rendering
milestones.note: Timer. Two numbers come out of one reading and they are deliberately not always the same number: a real <time> element carries an ISO 8601 duration in datetime and the human reading as its text, and past an hour the elapsed text stops showing seconds - at which point the duration follows the *text* rather than the raw elapsed time, because a duration that disagrees with its own visible reading is worse than none. The showcase renders two timers from the same start time to make that visible: the elapsed one reports a whole number of minutes while the clock one reports the true seconds. Nothing re-renders to keep the reading current - the hook owns the <time> node and writes only what changed, which the browser gate proves the only way it can be proven: it holds the node across a second and checks it is still the same node, since a re-render would have replaced it. The wait until the next change is computed against the precision the reading actually has, so past an hour this does not ask the clock every second to discover nothing moved. The discovery of this milestone is a platform one and it took the whole showcase page down: under js_of_ocaml an int is 32 bits, so milliseconds since 1970 do not fit in one and converting raises Invalid_argument. A JS number is a double and an OCaml float is a double, so start_time and the internal clock are floats - which is the faithful type on both sides, not a workaround. Core's Time_ns is unusable on this target for the same reason. The browser gate's 'the app mounted in Chromium' check is what caught it, from a page that had gone blank. Not ported: the theme seam, upstream's themeProps('timer') target - a theme can style the component's classes but cannot retarget its props.

milestones.name: a group of controls that reads as one field
milestones.note: InputGroup + InputGroupText. A labelled group: the label names the group rather than a control, so the port's Field omits the label's `for` (is_group_label, a parameter that existed before this milestone because FieldLabel was built with the group case in mind), and the status message is Detached, below the group, since there is no single control's edge for it to sit against. The size needs no plumbing: the group is inline-flex stretched to a step of the shared size scale, so its children fill the height. The two things upstream threads through React context are named divergences here rather than reproduced. InputGroupContext tells a nested input to render without its own label; this port's TextInput *requires* a label, so a control inside a group carries a visually hidden empty one - the caller's substitute, not an equivalent. SizeProvider is the same story from the other side: the caller knows the size it wants for its children, and the group's own box is CSS. React's ambient context re-enters through the DOM here - aria-* on the container and CSS on the box - and nowhere else, the same shape as ButtonGroup's connected look. Also not ported and named in the mli: labelTooltip, and the aria-describedby upstream puts on the group element (this port's Field does not hand back its description element's id, and inventing an id no element carries would be worse than its absence). Two build traps worth recording: Core defines a module named Field, so a sibling module must alias it as Field_ before the opens - text_area.ml and radio_list.ml already document this - and Vdom.Attr.class_ is variadic strings while Bonsai_web.Attr.class_ takes a list, which is the opposite of the lesson the earlier milestones recorded.

milestones.name: one tab stop for a bar of controls
milestones.note: Toolbar. A role=toolbar named by its label, navigated by the same roving tab stop ButtonGroup uses - now Common.List_focus, generalised with this component as its second consumer - and with the caret guard on, which is what lets a toolbar contain a text field: an arrow at the end of the input's text leaves the field and moves focus, an arrow with the caret mid-text moves the caret and leaves focus alone. Two slots layout in a flex row (start, end) and a centre slot switching the box to a three-column grid, so the middle is centred against the bar rather than against its neighbours. The gap reaches the slots through a variable on the box; role, aria-label and aria-orientation are stripped from the incoming props and set by the component, so a Toolbar cannot be handed a role that contradicts the behaviour inside it. Named divergences rather than approximations: the size is not passed down (no SizeContext here; the box takes the size scale's height and the caller builds its children knowing the size it wants - the same as InputGroup), useKeyboardHint (upstream's ephemeral arrow-key hint for sighted keyboard users, which would be a small self-contained follow-up since Kbd and the layer mechanism are already ported), and edge compensation (which lets a ghost button at an end sit flush against a container's edge).

milestones.name: terms and values whose layout belongs to the list
milestones.note: MetadataList + MetadataListItem. A real <dl> whose layout is chosen on the list and reaches the items as their container: the item renders the dt/dd pair as a fragment, so a single-column grid puts them on two rows (stacked) and a two-column grid puts them side by side, and no context travels between the two - the same resolution as InputGroup and ButtonGroup, for the same reason (a child is built before its container sees it). Six grids come out of columns x label position: auto minmax(0, 1fr), a responsive auto-fill at 280px, a 1fr single column when stacked, a wrapping flex row when horizontal, and an explicit repeat(N, ...) when columns is a number. Named divergences: no themeProps hook; the show-all toggle takes its two labels as arguments with English defaults and does not interpolate a hidden count the way upstream's i18n catalogue does; the id becomes the root's name as well as the content's. One difference follows from the fragment and is recorded rather than left to be discovered: upstream wraps a stacked pair in a flex column with a half-step gap, while a grid row gap is a full step, so a stacked pair sits slightly further apart here. A consequence worth knowing: the component is stateful whether or not anything truncates (upstream creates the state unconditionally and so does the port), so the jsdom harness cannot render it at all and its checks live in the browser gate, where the toggle can be clicked.

milestones.name: a delegation with nothing of its own
milestones.note: MoreMenu. 183 lines upstream that hold no behaviour: it is a DropdownMenu whose trigger is a ghost icon-only button, so it could only arrive after M23a made the menu configurable and controllable, and the port's version is that delegation with nothing invented in between. Divergences named: the label defaults to the English string the i18n catalogue holds; the default icon is the character because this port's icon set has no moreHorizontal glyph; hasChevron has no counterpart since the port's trigger renders no chevron at all; placement/alignment/presentation remain unported. The marker is passed down as the trigger's component_name, so the button the user sees says MoreMenu - a delegating component that did not name itself would be invisible to every tool here.

milestones.name: a value on a track, with marks that are reachable on their own
milestones.note: ProgressBar. The role sits on the *track* rather than the container, with the label outside it pointing in through aria-labelledby, so a label hidden from view still names the bar; the numbers (aria-valuenow/min/max and valuetext) are omitted entirely when the bar is indeterminate, because a point on a track with no position is not a point. Marks are labelled positions on the track: each is a focusable tick that stays *outside* the progressbar role, wrapped in the port's Tooltip (which is why the component takes a graph at all). Named divergences: upstream loads the mark tooltip lazily behind Suspense, which the port has no equivalent of; themeProps has no counterpart; and because the port cannot ask for a graph conditionally, a bar with no marks still takes one - so the jsdom gate cannot render this component and its checks live in the browser gate, where the fill's width is measured rather than read off a class.

milestones.name: a picture with a fallback, and a status a root role cannot prune away
milestones.note: Avatar, with AvatarStatusDot in the same directory (one coverage entry: the directory is the unit). Four display states in order - image, fallback source once the first failed, initials from the name, and the default icon when the name yields none, because the alternative is an empty plate. The accessible name is alt-or-name composed with the status's label, "Ada Lovelace, Online", because a role=img root prunes its descendants and the status would otherwise be unreachable. Upstream reads that label off the status element's props; OCaml cannot inspect a built node, so the port takes it as status_label. Named divergences: the hover tooltip is a title attribute, because the port's Tooltip takes a static trigger and this root is computed from the image state; the status's circle-mode edge offset is upstream's exact (1 - 1/sqrt 2)/2; the link-component seam is absent; and the image error chain is why this component takes a graph, so its checks live in the browser gate.

milestones.name: a facepile, and the margin that survives a wrapper
milestones.note: AvatarGroup, with AvatarGroupOverflow in the same directory (one coverage entry, as with Avatar). The overlap is upstream's round(size * 0.25), applied as a negative inline-start margin to every member *including the first* - upstream's reason, in upstream's comment, is that a negative container margin is defeated the moment a member is wrapped in something of its own, which is what a Tooltip does; the same wrapper problem the mark anchors hit in ProgressBar. Roving focus stands on Common.List_focus, already shared by ButtonGroup and Toolbar, and a screen reader is told through aria-describedby. The group does not measure: upstream's own docs say the consumer slices and passes an overflow chip, so there is no resize machinery here. Named divergences: size and shape are not propagated to members (the port has no contexts by design - the same rule that left Toolbar's SizeProvider named); the keyboard hint and the chip's label are English where upstream translates; themeProps has no counterpart. The group takes already-rendered avatars, which is what keeps it a function of nodes and lets the jsdom gate render it.

milestones.name: a button that stays down, and why it has to be a pure view
milestones.note: ToggleButton, with ToggleButtonGroup in the same directory (one coverage entry). It is the port's Button with aria-pressed, an icon that swaps while pressed, and - icon-only - the label doubling as the accessible name and the hover text. Upstream keeps its pressed context in a layer-scoped context (named divergence, like every other context), and reserves the pressed label's width with a second copy sharing a grid cell with the real one, which this Button's ~label API cannot express - named rather than faked, because a hidden in-flow copy widens the button instead of reserving it. The view is pure rather than graph-taking, and that is a design constraint rather than an accident: is_pressed is state the caller re-renders on, and a view that reached for the graph could not be re-run when it changed. The consequence is a bonus - the component is static, so the jsdom gate renders it, and the tooltip becomes a title (the same call Avatar made, for the same reason).

milestones.name: the card that carries its own checkbox, and what is not in it
milestones.note: SelectableCard: a Card with selection on top, and a visually-hidden <input type=checkbox> inside carrying the role, the accessible name and the checked state, so the card surface is a plain <div> with no role and no tabindex. The click rules are ported literally, because they are the mechanism: a surface click toggles, a click on a nested interactive element is left alone (upstream's INTERACTIVE_SELECTORS list, ported as a shared constant), and a click that ends a text selection is ignored so dragging to select a card's text never changes the selection. Enter is added by hand and Space is not, because a native checkbox already answers Space and adding it would toggle twice. Card gained ?component_name and ?attrs, mirroring Button's delegation marker: upstream stamps 'selectable-card' rather than inheriting Card's, and every tool in this repo identifies a component by that marker, so a wrapper that keeps its delegate's name is invisible to all of them. NOT ported, and named: the touch press model (utils/pressFeedback.ts, 461 lines plus its gesture module and CSS arms) - the contract attribute is emitted and the mouse press paints through :active, and a touch press does not, because that model is a campaign on the scale of Layer, not a milestone.

milestones.name: a card whose whole surface is the action, and the second consumer that proved the mechanism
milestones.note: ClickableCard: a Card plus one visually-hidden interactive element - an <a> when there is an href, a <button> when there is not - carrying the accessible name, so the surface needs no role of its own and the card is operable as a link or a button. Its click rules are the same mechanism SelectableCard was carrying, which made this the second consumer and moved the interactive-target test, the text-selection rule and the selector list into Common.Clickable_container - a mechanism move, proved by the existing suites passing unchanged and moving no coverage number (committed separately, 3da85f8). One substantive difference from copying the JSX: the href ATTRIBUTE is gated by the port's safe-url predicate, not only the navigation. Upstream hands its href to a framework link component and React vets the hrefs it writes as attributes; nothing here passes through React, so an unvetted attribute would be a live sink even though this component's own click path refuses it. A refused value renders inert - no href, role=link, aria-disabled, tabindex=-1 - which is the rule the rest of the port already follows. Navigation picks the safe-url predicate up from Citation, where the port put its security control. Named divergences: the touch press model (as SelectableCard), and a native <a> in place of a framework link component, so navigation is a real document navigation rather than a client-side transition.

ported.note: one module, three kinds (checkbox, radio, bare check) — upstream's registry default, with the theme-override seam not ported yet

M45. Divergence: the OCaml module is Astryx.List_container (renamed because a top-level module named List shadows Stdlib/Core in this effectively-unwrapped library — the 'List' name is un-addressable; empirically src/list.ml -> dependency cycle Vstack → Common → List → Common). List_item is the row builder. divergent_module: true.

M46. Divergences (recorded in src/tree_list.ml): on_click is unit -> unit (house API) rather than a DOM event; the toggle aria-label is English "Toggle children" (upstream i18n); per-item xstyle/className/style have no counterpart (port emits BEM class names). Tree_focus is a separate module (port of upstream hooks/useTreeFocus.ts); Tree_branches is private.

M47. Draft-commit semantics: the text is a draft until blur or Enter (upstream's commit-on-blur/Enter policy), only valid numbers reach on_change, blank commits as empty, out-of-range clamps to min/max on commit. Locale-aware decimal parser, wheel support off by default. Divergences: status is the house Input_types record, units/format_value are OCaml-level, no React node in description.

M48. Collection mode (value : string list Bonsai.t / on_change), rows built here rather than through List_item because a row's checkbox must read the list's value (divergence recorded in src/checkbox_list.mli). changeAction not portable to Bonsai — per-item is_loading instead. Row-surface click delegation replicates upstream useClickableContainer; the visible label is a span (the checkbox is named once by its own hidden label). Group-disabled-with-message keeps every box focusable (aria-disabled + form="", is_focusable_disabled on Checkbox_input.render) with one reason bubble for the set. Standalone CheckboxListItem, rich ReactNode labels, xstyle/className/style not ported.
